# Sodium Phosphate

Phosphate loading before competition, an old idea with a stubbornly inconsistent literature. Some trials show aerobic gains, others show nothing at all.

## At a glance

What the evidence covers
: - Aerobic capacity gains in some trials Limited evidence
- No effect on time-trial performance in others Limited evidence
- Repeated-sprint results are mixed Limited evidence
Studied dose
: Loading protocols use about 3–4 g/day of sodium phosphate split into four doses for 3–6 days before competition, with several weeks of washout between loads.
Safety
: GI upset is common.

Where to buy

Limited evidence — few or small studies, or mostly negative results. Grade assigned under our published criteria: How we grade evidence.

## Before you buy: stronger evidence for the same goal

The evidence for this supplement is limited. These alternatives target the same goal with better research behind them: (for high-intensity performance, the evidence is stronger for these)

- Sodium Bicarbonate Strong evidence
- Beta-Alanine Moderate evidence
- Beetroot (Dietary Nitrate) Moderate evidence

## What the science says

- Aerobic capacity gains in some trials Limited evidence

A randomised, placebo-controlled crossover study in cyclists found short-term phosphate loading improved aerobic capacity under acute hypoxia, with related work reporting changes in cardiorespiratory responses. Results in normoxia have been less consistent.
- No effect on time-trial performance in others Limited evidence

A randomised trial found sodium phosphate did not improve 20 km cycling time-trial performance or the main physiological responses to submaximal exercise.
- Repeated-sprint results are mixed Limited evidence

Randomised trials of phosphate loading for repeated-sprint ability, alone or combined with other ergogenic aids, produced small and inconsistent effects.

## Dosage & safety

Studied dose Loading protocols use about 3–4 g/day of sodium phosphate split into four doses for 3–6 days before competition, with several weeks of washout between loads.

Safety GI upset is common. High phosphate intake is genuinely risky in kidney disease and can disturb calcium balance, so repeated loading is not advised. It also adds a meaningful sodium load.

## How to take it

Timing Split it into four doses spread across the day during the loading block.

With food? Take each dose with food and fluid, which is the main way to limit the GI upset.

Worth knowing Check you are buying dibasic sodium phosphate, not the sodium phosphate sold as a bowel-prep laxative.

### With medications

- blood-pressure and heart failure medication

The sodium load pushes against sodium restriction and diuretic therapy. do not load phosphate if you take these without medical approval
- phosphate binders, calcitriol and other drugs managing calcium-phosphate balance

A deliberate phosphate load directly undermines the treatment. do not combine; this is unsafe in kidney disease

### With other supplements

- calcium supplements

Calcium and phosphate bind each other in the gut, cutting absorption of both. separate them by at least 2 hours

Well-established interactions only — this is not a complete list. Always tell your doctor and pharmacist what you take.

## Frequently asked questions

Does phosphate loading improve endurance?

Sodium phosphate loading has limited, inconsistent evidence: some trials show aerobic capacity gains, especially in hypoxia, while another found no improvement in 20 km cycling time-trial performance. Repeated-sprint results with sodium phosphate are also mixed.

How do you phosphate load with sodium phosphate?

Sodium phosphate loading protocols use about 3–4 g/day split into four doses with food and fluid for 3–6 days before competition, with several weeks between loads. Buy dibasic sodium phosphate, not the sodium phosphate sold as a bowel-prep laxative.

Is sodium phosphate loading safe?

Stomach upset is common with sodium phosphate, and high phosphate intake is genuinely risky in kidney disease and can disturb calcium balance, so repeated loading is not advised. Sodium phosphate also adds a meaningful sodium load, which works against blood pressure and heart failure treatment.

Can I take sodium phosphate with calcium?

Calcium and phosphate bind each other in the gut, cutting absorption of both, so separate sodium phosphate from calcium supplements by at least 2 hours.
